note: SGSM3 loss-of-function variants have been linked to autosomal recessive intellectual disability in very small cohorts, making the hypothesis of loss-of-function pathogenicity plausible.

evidence.text: A homozygous stop-gain variation (p.Arg526Ter) in SGSM3 was identified in two siblings with intellectual disability and short stature, supporting loss-of-function variants causing the recessive phenotype across limited cohorts.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: In this study, a novel homozygous stop-gain (NM_015705.6: c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) variation was detected in the SGSM3 gene in two siblings with short stature and ID findings. The report of two cases with bi-allelic LOF variants in the SGSM3 gene from different populations with similar clinical manifestations strengthens the potential of this gene as a candidate gene for the nonsyndromic ID phenotype.

evidence.text: SGSM3 was reported as a candidate disease gene for autosomal recessive mild to moderate intellectual disability and short stature harboring a homozygous founder variant in Ashkenazi Jews.

source.title: Intellectual disability syndrome associated with a homozygous founder variant in SGSM3 in Ashkenazi Jews
source.quote: In this paper, we highlight SGSM3 as a candidate disease gene for autosomal recessive mild to moderate intellectual disability. We identified a founder variant in Ashkenazi Jews
